assessmentSummary.identity: One Foot Tripod Weight Shift repetition is a bilateral standing four-direction circuit. Start centered with both heels, first metatarsal heads, fifth metatarsal heads, and relaxed toes in contact on a clean dry level surface. Shift the body mass forward until pressure increases under the forefeet without either heel lifting, return to center, shift backward without either forefoot losing contact, return to center, shift left without stepping, return to center, then shift right without stepping and return to the same centered stance. Keep every tripod contact connected, toes relaxed, knees soft and body control quiet. One complete forward, backward, left, and right circuit with all four returns is one repetition. The wall-touch version is an exact support variant. Direction-only tasks, stepping, gait, single-leg support, reaching, ankle-only rocking, short-foot doming, toe pressing, heel raising, unstable surfaces, external load, biofeedback, maximal limits testing, or clinical treatment change the variant or definition.
currentCardFindings: Source 47 has one stable legacy definition but its source variant is skeletal and does not define the four-direction sequence, center returns, contact validity, support option, pressure versus contact boundary, fatigue, duration, substitutions, or review state.

The task is not a short-foot, hallux-press, balance-hold, or heel-raise exercise. It deliberately changes pressure under a fixed bilateral base while preserving contacts and does not claim that contact means constant pressure.

assessmentSummary.identity: One Big Toe Press Iso Hold repetition is performed on one target foot. Start with the target heel, first and fifth metatarsal heads, relaxed hallux, and lesser toes supported on a clean dry level surface. Press the hallux plantarward into the surface to a comfortable prescribed submaximal effort without curling the lesser toes, lifting the heel or metatarsal heads, rolling the foot, or turning the task into an arch dome. assessmentSummary.identity: One Short Foot to Calf Raise repetition is performed from a bilateral standing base. Start with both heels, first metatarsal heads, fifth metatarsal heads, and relaxed long toes supported on a clean dry level surface. Gently create a short-foot arch on both feet by drawing the metatarsal heads toward the heels without curling or lifting the toes. Maintain the forefoot contacts while rising directly upward into a comfortable bilateral heel raise, pause only as prescribed, lower both heels with control to the same flat-foot start, then fully relax the short-foot action before the next repetition. The heel is expected to leave contact during the rise; first and fifth metatarsal head contact and quiet toe behavior remain required. Standing hands-free and light wall-touch are exact variants. Single-leg, step, seated, bent-knee, externally loaded, sustained-top-hold, rebound, toe-dorsiflexed, manually assisted, resistance-on-midfoot, or clinical treatment forms change the variant or definition.
